| [LIT-616](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-616.md) | A Widely Applicable Bayesian Information Criterion | Watanabe (2012), arXiv:1208.6338; JMLR 14:867–897 (2013). A model is singular when the parameter-to-distribution map is not one-to-one or the Fisher information is not positive definite: neural networks, mixtures, reduced-rank regression, HMMs. Its Bayes free energy is nL_n(w0) + λ log n − (m − 1) log log n + O_p(1), with λ the real log canonical threshold (RLCT), not d/2. WBIC, the posterior average of nL_n(w) at inverse temperature 1/log n, has the same leading terms even for singular, unrealizable models, equals BIC for regular ones, and needs no knowledge of the true distribution. Two temperatures give an estimate of λ. In reduced-rank regression WBIC picked the true rank in 100 of 100 trials and recovered theoretical RLCTs closely. | Active — read in full 2026-10-03 ([NOTE-473](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-473.md)); worth reading as the record's lawful, short statement of the core of singular learning theory, standing in for Watanabe's unread book ([LIT-354](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-354.md)). Its own result is WBIC, the posterior mean of nL_n(w) at inverse temperature 1/log n, which matches F to the λ log n term even for singular and unrealizable models (Theorem 4), equals BIC for regular ones (Theorem 5), and estimates λ from two temperatures (Corollary 3). | [LIT-620](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-620.md) | Post hoc Bayesian model selection | Friston & Penny (2011), NeuroImage 56(4):2089–2099. | [LIT-623](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-623.md) v2 | Bayesian Interpolation | MacKay (1992), Neural Computation 4(3):415–447. Two levels of inference: fit each model, then rank models by their evidence P(D\|H). | [LIT-3114](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3114.md) | Regulation of choice behavior: an experiment investigating the hypothesis that people bundle sequences of expected rewards | Schuhr (2015), a UCT doctoral thesis, designed with George Ainslie. A between-session experiment (n = 29-37 per treatment) with real payouts: choices presented as a series of paired decisions made at once, with no constraint between them, were more often larger-later than the same choices presented singly, and a mixture model put 31 points more probability on exponential discounting with bundling. Forcing the decisions to match lowered that probability.
